s: Which electronic device was used in Second Generation Computers?
x: Transistors were used in the second generation computers. A second generation computer, is a type of computer that, as opposed to vacuum tubes (of first generation computers), relies on descrete transistors as its principal component to do the processing.

s: ICs are classified on the basis of :
x: ICs can be classified on the basis of their chip size as given below : Small Scale Integration (SSI) – 3 to 30 transistors/chips Medium Scale Integration (MSI) – 30 to 300 transistors/chips Large Scale Integration (LSI) – 300 to 3,000 transistors/chip Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) – more than 3000 transistors/chip.

s: Miniaturization of present day computers has been possible due to the use of –
x: Integrated circuit is a set of electronic circuits on one small plate of semiconductor material normally silicon. After its invention in 1958, it is used in place of transistors in the computer and hence we can say that the miniaturization of present day computers has been possible due to these integrated circuit units.

s: Who is considered to be the ‘Father of Computers’?
x: Charles Babbage, who designed the Analytical Engine, is called the Father of Computers. Tim Berners-Lee is known for the WWW.

s: Which one of the following person has produced the first portable computer?
x: Adam Osborne produced the first commercial portable computer, the Osborne 1 (1981); the other names are not associated with it.

s: Who is internationally recognised as a father of the modern digital computer?
x: George Stibitz, the Bell Labs engineer who built the relay-based binary digital calculator in 1937, is internationally recognised as a father of the modern digital computer.

s: In the field of computing, what does ENIAC stand for?
x: ENIAC stands for Electronic Numerical Integrator And Computer, the first general-purpose electronic computer (1946).

s: Which one of the following has developed the C-language for the computer for the first time?
x: Dennis Ritchie developed the C language.

s: Which one of the following persons created the Java programming language in 1994?
x: James Gosling created Java.

s: Who among the following, the creator of the world's first portable computer, died at Kodaikanal on March 18, 2003?
x: Adam Osborne created the Osborne 1, the world's first portable computer, and died in Kodaikanal in 2003.

s: Who invented electronic computer?
x: Colossus was the name of a series of electronic digital computer developed for British code breakers in 1943-1945 to help in the cryptanalysis of the Lorenz Cipher. It was designed by the British engineer Tommy Flowers. Alan Mathison Turing also contributed to its design but the fact was that he was not directly involved in it. But in the available options, Dr. Alan M. Turing is the correct answer.

s: Who invented the computer mouse?
x: Douglas Engelbart invented the mouse; Larry Tesler is credited with cut, copy and paste.

s: Who is regarded as the first computer programmer?

x: Silicon is the semiconductor from which integrated circuit chips are made.

x: Tim Berners-Lee invented the WWW in 1989; Engelbart invented the mouse.

s: Which type of computer could be found in a digital watch?
x: An embedded system is a computer system with a dedicated function within a larger mechanical or electrical system often with real-time computing constraints. It is embedded as part of a complete device often including hardware and mechanical parts. Embedded systems control many devices in common use today. Embedded systems range from portable devices such as digital watches and MP3 players to large stationary installations like traffic lights, factory controllers and largely complex systems like hybrid vehicles, MRI, and avionics.

s: Which of the following is an example of a hybrid computer?

s: What do quantum computers use to process information?
x: Quantum computers use qubits, which rely on superposition and entanglement.

s: The most important part of a computer is –
x: Central Processing Unit (C.P.U.) is the most important part of a computer. Here computer analyzes the received information or data.

s: Which part of Central Processing Unit (CPU) performs calculations and makes decisions?
x: Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is responsible for performing calculations and contains decision-making mechanisms. In the computer system, ALU is a main component of the central processing unit (CPU), which performs all arithmetic and logic operations that must be performed on instruction words.

CPU – refers to Control Processing Unit
ALU – refers to Arithmetic Logic Unit
x: CPU refers to 'Central Processing Unit'. It is the brain of the computer where most of the calculations take place. Statements of other three options are correct.

s: On which principle digital computer works ?
x: All digital computers rely on binary system of 1 and 0 and on the rules of logic set out in the 1850s by English mathematician George Boole. Just three operations (AND, OR and NOT) can perform all logical functions known as Boolean Logic.

s: In a computer, which unit is responsible for processing data and is also called the electronic brain of the computer?
x: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain of the computer where most processing happens. RAM, keyboard and hard disk are memory, input and storage devices.

s:

II. The CPU is the software within a computer system which carries out the instructions of a computer program.

x: Statement I is correct: the CPU is the brain and most important part. Statement II is wrong because the CPU is hardware, not software.

s: The computer’s processor consists which of the following parts?
Which of the following is function of Control Unit in CPU?
x: The Control Unit (CU) is an internal component of the microprocessor architecture that generates the necessary control signals to execute the program instructions and to control the various operations performed by the processor. The CPU (processor) contains three functional units. These functional units are Control Unit (CU), Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) and the Memory Unit (MU). It is the CU that decodes the program instructions and control and directs all the operations of the computer system.

s: Which is the fastest storage inside the CPU?
x: Registers are the fastest storage, followed by cache and then RAM.

s: Which component of the CPU fetches and decodes program instructions?
x: The control unit fetches, decodes and directs; the ALU does arithmetic and logic, and the PSU only supplies power.

s: What is the full form of CPU?
x: CPU is the Central (not Control) Processing Unit, the brain of the computer.

s: What is the full form of UPS?
x: UPS (Uninterrupted Power Supply) keeps the computer running briefly when the power fails.

s: What is the full form of SMPS?
x: SMPS (Switched Mode Power Supply) changes rectified AC input into low-voltage DC.

s: What is the full form of IBM?
x: IBM stands for International Business Machines.

s: How many cores does the high-end Intel Core i9 CPU have?
x: Intel Core i9 is a high-end multi-core CPU with 8 to 24 cores.

s: After a double-click of the mouse, where does the information go?
x: After a double-click, the information goes to the CPU, which processes it.

x: Random Access Memory (RAM) is the hardware in a computing device that provides temporary storage for the operating system (OS), software programs and any other data in current use so they're quickly available to the device's processor. Random access memory is considered part of a computer's primary memory. It is much faster to read from and write to than secondary storage, such as hard disk drives (HDDs), solid-state drives (SSDs) or optical drives. However, RAM is volatile; it retains data only as long as the computer is on. If power is lost, so is the data. When the computer is rebooted, the OS and other files must be reloaded into RAM, usually from an HDD or SSD. Hence, statement of option (b) is not true about RAM, while statements of other three options are correct.

s: Which is not a type of secondary memory?
x: Solid State Drive, Hard Disk and USB Pen Drive are types of computer's external or secondary memory while Random Access Memory (RAM) is part of computer's internal or primary memory.

s: Which of the following memory of the computer is used to speed up the computer processing?
x: Cache memory is the fastest memory in a computer and is used to speed up the computer processing. It is used to speed up access to data and applications. It is built into the CPU and is typically integrated onto the motherboard.

s: The content of computer memory which is non-volatile, even when the power goes off is :
x: Non-volatile computer memory retains data even when power is removed, examples include ROM (Read-Only Memory), flash memory (like in SSDs and USB drives), and hard disk drives.

s: In a computer, the permanent memory is called –
x: ROM is considered as the permanent memory of computer. Data or information in ROM is not destroyed or erased even after the computer is turned off.

s: Basic Input-Output system in computer resides :
x: The Basic Input-Output system in computer resides on the ROM.

s: Size of virtual memory depends on –
x: The size of virtual memory (the virtual address space) is determined by the number of CPU address lines, e.g. 32 address lines give 2^32 bytes; disc space only limits the backing store.

s: Which one of the following is not correct statement about 'Flash memory' ?
o: It is used for information storage in devices like digital
It can operate in extended temperature range of – 400C
It is cheaper than the normal mechanical disk drives
x: 'Flash memory' which is used in computers and other digital bodies or devices is a type of memory that persists even when the power is off. Pen drive, digital camera, and memory card are the examples of flash memory. In comparison to the hard drive, a flash memory is much energy efficient. But if we compare in the terms of per unit storage of flash drive, it is expensive than normal hard drive.

s: How many bits are there in a kilobyte?
x: A byte contains 8 bit and 1 kilobyte (KB) contains 1024 bytes. Like this – 1 kilobyte = 1024 × 8 bits = 8192 bits. Geopbyte containing 1024 Brontobytes is the largest storage unit.

s: How many bits are there in one byte?
x: One byte consists of 8 bits, so the answer is 8.

s: Which of the following is an extremely fast, small memory between CPU and main memory?
x: Cache memory is an extremely fast, small memory between CPU and main memory. It stores data from a computer or program that is often used by the CPU.

s: Which secondary storage is sequential-access and mainly used for backup and archival?
x: Magnetic tape is sequential-access, the slowest in the speed order, and used for backup and archival; an SSD uses flash memory with no moving parts.

s: How many bits make a nibble?
x: A nibble is a group of four bits.

s: Which type of RAM is used as cache memory?
x: SRAM is used as cache, while DRAM is used as main memory.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: EEPROM — erasable only by ultraviolet light
x: EPROM is erased using ultraviolet light. EEPROM is electrically erasable, while ROM is non-volatile.

s:
Consider the following statements about memory:
1. EEPROM is erased electrically.
2. DRAM is used as cache memory.
3. BIOS is held in ROM.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: EEPROM is erased electrically and BIOS resides in ROM; cache is SRAM, while DRAM is main memory.

s: How much data can a single-layer DVD store?
x: A single-layer DVD holds 4.7 GB (8.5 GB dual layer); a CD holds about 700 MB.

s: How much data can a single-layer Blu-ray disc store?
x: A single-layer Blu-ray holds 25 GB; dual layer holds 50 GB.

s: Which storage uses flash memory and has no moving parts?
x: An SSD uses flash memory with no moving parts and is faster than an HDD.

s: How much is 1 TB equal to?
x: 1 TB = 1024 GB, and 1 GB = 1024 MB.

s:
Consider the following statements about secondary storage:
1. Magnetic tape is sequential-access and the slowest storage.
2. A flash drive is cheaper than mechanical disks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Magnetic tape is sequential and slowest; flash drives are not cheaper than mechanical disks.

s: Which memory is erased by ultraviolet light?
x: EPROM is erased by ultraviolet light; EEPROM is erased electrically.

s: What is the full form of DIMM?
x: DIMM is the Dual In-line Memory Module, a RAM stick with contacts on both sides.

s: What is the full form of BIOS?
x: BIOS (Basic Input-Output System) is firmware held in ROM.

s: About how much data can a CD store?
x: A CD holds about 700 MB; a single-layer DVD 4.7 GB and a single-layer Blu-ray 25 GB.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: A device driver is system software, not application software.

s: Which of the following statements about open-source software is correct?
o: It is limited to operating systems produced by one company.
Its source code is permanently hidden from users.
It can never be commercially distributed.
Its source code is free to view, modify and share, subject to its licence.
x: Open-source software makes source code available for viewing, modification and sharing under the applicable licence.

s: Antivirus, disk cleanup and backup programs are examples of which type of software?
x: Antivirus, disk cleanup, backup and compression tools are utility software.

s: Oracle, MySQL and MS Access are examples of which application software?
x: Oracle, MySQL and MS Access are database software; Photoshop and CorelDRAW are graphics software.

s: What is the full form of GNU?
x: GNU stands for 'GNU's Not Unix'; it is free, Unix-like OS software.

s:
Consider the following statements about software:
1. Internet Explorer is closed (proprietary) software.
2. Microsoft Office is an operating system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Internet Explorer is closed source; Microsoft Office is an office suite, not an OS.

s: Which type of software is a device driver?
x: Device drivers are system software, along with the OS and translators.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Software)
A. Adobe Photoshop
B. MySQL
C. MS Outlook
D. Antivirus
List-II (Type)
1. Database software
2. Graphics software
3. Utility software
4. E-mail application
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Photoshop is graphics software, MySQL database software, MS Outlook handles e-mail, and antivirus is utility software.

s: WordStar, from MicroPro International, is an example of which type of software?
x: WordStar, like Microsoft Word, is word processing software.

s: What does the extension of a computer file, such as .doc, show?
o: The date the file was made
x: The extension shows the file type; .doc is a Word document.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of operating systems?
o: Real-time operating systems have no fixed response deadlines
In a time-sharing OS such as UNIX, many users share CPU time
Real-time operating systems are used in missile guidance and air-traffic control
A batch OS groups jobs and runs them without user interaction
x: Real-time OS work to fixed response deadlines, which is why they are used for missile guidance and air-traffic control.

s: On which operating system is Android, associated with Google, based?
x: Android is Linux-based and associated with Google; iOS is Apple's, and BharOS was developed at IIT Madras.

s: Missile guidance and air-traffic control systems use which type of operating system?
x: Real-time OSs work to fixed response deadlines, as in missile guidance and air-traffic control.

s: Who developed the mobile operating system BharOS?
x: BharOS is from IIT Madras; Android is Google's and iOS is Apple's.

s: Who wrote MS-DOS from 86-DOS?
x: Tim Paterson wrote MS-DOS from 86-DOS; Microsoft released it in August 1981.

s: Which of the following operating systems uses a graphical user interface (GUI)?
x: Windows and macOS use a GUI; MS-DOS and the UNIX shell are command-line interfaces.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNIX?
o: It is a multi-user operating system
It was made in 1969 by AT&T
Its main part is the kernel
It is a mobile operating system by Google
x: UNIX is a multi-user OS made in 1969 by AT&T with the kernel as its main part; Android is Google's mobile OS.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: CLI — icons and windows controlled mainly by a mouse
x: MS-DOS is associated with a command-line interface. GUIs use icons, windows and mouse interaction, as in Windows and macOS.

s: In which year was the UNIX operating system made at AT&T?
x: UNIX, a multi-user OS, was made in 1969 at AT&T; MS-DOS came in 1981 and Linux in 1991.

s: Which of the following is NOT a function of an operating system?
o: Translating a high-level program line by line
x: Line-by-line translation is done by an interpreter; the OS manages hardware, memory, files, processes and the user interface.

s: In which year was Windows 11 released?
x: Windows 11 was released in October 2021; Windows 3 came in 1990.

s: Which among the following is not an operating system?
x: UNIX, Android and MS-DOS are operating systems; COBOL is a programming language.

s: Select the odd one out:
x: Windows, macOS and Linux are operating systems; Java is a programming language.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about assembly language?
o: It is converted into machine code by a compiler
It is converted into machine code by an assembler
x: Assembly language uses mnemonics and is converted into machine code by an assembler, not a compiler.

s: What is a language translator that translates and runs a program line by line called?
x: An interpreter translates and executes line by line, while a compiler translates the whole program before execution.

s: Which of the following are known as universal gates?
x: NAND and NOR are the universal gates; AND, OR and NOT are the basic gates.

s: By what name is the Boolean identity (A + B)′ = A′ · B′ known?
x: (A + B)′ = A′ · B′ is De Morgan's law.

s: What is the pictorial representation of an algorithm called?
x: A flowchart is the pictorial form of an algorithm, which is a finite step-by-step procedure (APPSC 2019). Pseudocode is an English-like text outline, a compiler is a language translator, and source code is the written program.

s: What is the decimal value of the hexadecimal number (FF)₁₆?
x: F represents 15, so FF equals 15 × 16 + 15 = 255.

s: Who created the Python programming language?
x: Guido van Rossum created Python; Gosling made Java, Ritchie C and Stroustrup C++.

s: In what way does a compiler differ from an interpreter?
o: Translates and runs line by line
Translates the whole program at once
x: A compiler translates the whole program at once; an interpreter works line by line.

s: In a flowchart, which symbol shows a decision?
x: Diamond = decision; oval = start/end, parallelogram = input/output, rectangle = process.

s: What is an English-like text outline of a program's logic called?
x: Pseudocode is an English-like outline; a flowchart is the pictorial form of an algorithm.

s: When does an XOR gate give output 1?
x: XOR gives 1 only when its inputs differ.

s: What is the decimal value of the binary number (1010)₂?
Which of the following is NOT a computer programming language?
x: Linux is an operating system; COBOL, Java and FORTRAN are programming languages.

s: What is the full form of FORTRAN?
x: FORTRAN = Formula Translation; it was made by IBM for scientific work.

s: Which was the first high-level programming language, developed by IBM in 1957?
x: FORTRAN (1957, IBM) was the first high-level language; COBOL is for business.

s: What is the full form of BASIC?
o: Beginner's All Purpose Symbolic Instruction Code
Binary All Purpose Symbolic Instruction Code
x: BASIC stands for Beginner's All Purpose Symbolic Instruction Code; it is a procedural language.

s: In a flowchart, which symbol is used for input or output?
x: In a flowchart, oval = start/end, parallelogram = input/output, rectangle = process and diamond = decision.

s: Who created the C++ programming language?
x: Bjarne Stroustrup created C++; Ritchie made C, Gosling Java and van Rossum Python.

s: Which digits are used in the hexadecimal number system?
x: Hexadecimal is base 16 and uses 0-9 and A-F.

s: What is the base of the hexadecimal number system?
x: Hexadecimal is base 16; binary is base 2, octal 8 and decimal 10.

s: In Boolean algebra, what is the value of A + A?
x: By the idempotent law A + A = A.

s: In Boolean algebra, what is the value of A · A′ (A AND NOT A)?
x: A variable ANDed with its complement always gives 0: A · A′ = 0.

s: Which high-level language is mainly used for business applications?
x: COBOL is the business language; FORTRAN is for scientific work.

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. FORTRAN – Scientific work
2. COBOL – Business applications
3. BASIC – Beginner's All Purpose Symbolic Instruction Code
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
x: All three pairs are correct: FORTRAN is scientific, COBOL is for business and BASIC is Beginner's All Purpose Symbolic Instruction Code.

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its file type?
x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format. MP3 is audio, PDF is a document format and MOV is a video format.

s: How many bits does ASCII, the character-encoding scheme for 128 characters, use?
x: ASCII is a 7-bit code (2^7 = 128 characters); Unicode extends its range.

s: The communication from a computer mouse to the computer is an example of which transmission mode?
x: A mouse only sends signals to the computer, so the communication is one-way, or simplex (APPSC 2019). Half duplex is two-way but one direction at a time, as in a walkie-talkie. Full duplex is two-way at once, as in a telephone. Multiplexing combines several signals on one channel; it is not a direction mode.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics, not Portable Network Graphics Interface. AVI, MOV and GIF are correctly matched.

s: What is the full form of PDF?
x: PDF is Adobe's Portable Document Format.

s: Which company developed the AVI (Audio Video Interleave) format?
x: AVI is Microsoft's; MOV is Apple's, PDF Adobe's and GIF CompuServe's.

s: A telephone call is an example of which transmission mode?
x: A telephone is full duplex; television is simplex and a walkie-talkie half duplex.

s: For which type of content is MP3 a file format?
x: MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer 3) is an audio format; MP4, MOV and AVI are video formats.

s: What is the full form of JPEG?
x: JPEG = Joint Photographic Experts Group; it is a lossy image format.

s: Which of the following is an example of half-duplex communication?
x: In half duplex, data flows both ways but one at a time, as in a walkie-talkie; television is simplex and telephone full duplex.

s: By which process does an LED produce light?
x: An LED (Light Emitting Diode) gives light by electroluminescence at a semiconductor p-n junction.

s: What is the full form of ASCII?
o: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Standard Code for International Interchange
Advanced Standard Code for Information Interchange
American Symbolic Code for Information Interchange
x: ASCII = American Standard Code for Information Interchange; a 7-bit code for 128 characters.

s: Which character-encoding standard extends the 7-bit ASCII code?
x: ASCII is 7-bit with 128 characters; Unicode extends it.

s: In which unit is the speed of a supercomputer commonly expressed?
x: Supercomputers provide the highest processing power, and their speed is commonly expressed in FLOPS (floating-point operations per second).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about computer performance terms?
o: Bandwidth is the data-transfer rate, measured in bits per second
Word length is the number of bits the CPU handles at once
Clock speed is measured in bits per second
MIPS stands for million instructions per second
x: Clock speed is measured in hertz (GHz); bits per second is the unit of bandwidth.

s: Which benchmark measures floating-point performance while solving large dense linear systems and forms the basis of world supercomputer rankings?
x: The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.

s: Which is the world's fastest supercomputer according to the ISC 2026 list?
x: China's LineShine topped the ISC 2026 supercomputer list, replacing the United States' El Capitan.

s: Where was the 3.1-petaflop supercomputer Param Shakti launched by MeitY?
x: Param Shakti, funded under the National Supercomputing Mission, was launched by MeitY at IIT Madras.

s: In which unit is bandwidth, the data-transfer rate, measured?
x: Bandwidth is measured in bits per second; clock speed is in hertz.

s: What is the full form of MIPS?
x: MIPS = Million Instructions Per Second.

s:
Consider the following statements about Param Shakti:
1. It is a 3.1-petaflop supercomputer.
2. It was launched at IIT Madras.
3. It was built under the Digital India Mission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Param Shakti (3.1 petaflops) was launched by MeitY at IIT Madras under the National Supercomputing Mission.

s: Which Indian supercomputer, built by CRL (Tata), was ranked 4th in the world in November 2007?
x: Eka of CRL (Tata) was ranked 4th in November 2007, when IBM Blue Gene/L was the fastest.

s: Which was the world's fastest supercomputer in 2007, when India's Eka ranked 4th?
x: In 2007 IBM Blue Gene/L was the fastest; India's Eka (CRL, Tata) was 4th in November 2007.

s: Which one of the following was the first commercial microprocessor?
x: The Intel 4004, introduced in 1971, was the first commercial microprocessor.
